principle: A story pattern is a decision path, not a fixed page layout. Select one dominant pattern and at most two supporting patterns; never assemble one module per feature.

patterns.name: Feature-led
patterns.consumer_trigger: The category is already understood and shoppers compare a familiar set of functions.
use: Bundle many functions into one hierarchy before assigning visuals
Use chapters for coherent feature families
Reserve comparison and support for the end
adapt: Limit feature clusters to one consumer question per visual
Alternate at least one human scenario with technical chapters

patterns.name: Category Education
patterns.consumer_trigger: The product category, workflow or reason to buy is unfamiliar.
use: Explain the user task before technical vocabulary
Turn abstract AI or wellness value into visible outputs
Repeat the product after education so it remains a physical purchase
adapt: Use SwitchBot user language and approved product UI
Keep education visual and short enough for Amazon scanning
avoid: Claiming category leadership without approved evidence
Treating lifestyle scenes as technical proof

patterns.name: Performance-led
patterns.consumer_trigger: A measurable or observable result is the main reason to switch or pay more.
use: Put comparison conditions beside performance claims
Connect numbers to visible user outcomes
Break one major USP into specific failure-point proofs
adapt: Reduce every proof to one result, one mechanism and one source
Use clean SwitchBot technical diagrams rather than dense ecommerce collages

patterns.name: Scenario-led
patterns.consumer_trigger: Fit, routine or emotional context matters more than raw specifications.
use: Choose scenes that answer a purchase question
Keep the official product layer visually accurate
Use scenarios to validate fit after the core value is understood
adapt: Use believable Japanese homes and work contexts
Separate AI or stock scene layers from the official product layer
avoid: Hiding the product to achieve mood

patterns.name: Technology-led
patterns.consumer_trigger: The purchase depends on understanding an invisible mechanism, platform or system relationship.
use: Start with the user benefit before naming the technology
Use programmatic diagrams and source-linked labels
Show one lived consequence after each technical chapter
adapt: Use dark contrast only for selected proof moments
Translate expert detail into Japanese consumer questions
avoid: Invented UI, connector relationships or technical labels
